title: KV cache consistency: chaos-validation and rollback matrix
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
=======
This document defines a focused validation and rollback matrix for KV (key-value) cache state consistency in Redwood private deployments. It is intended for operator teams validating upgrades, runtime changes (quantization, kernel swaps), and chaos experiments that touch cache topology or eviction behavior. The goal is to provide repeatable checks, acceptance criteria, and a clear rollback decision matrix so customer-facing Private deployments maintain correctness and SLOs during day-2 activities.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood Private control plane + runtime instances that use the distributed KV cache (local LRU + tiered remote backing).
- Covers: cache population/eviction, hot-swap of model shards, cross-node cache invalidation, and forced eviction/GC scenarios.
- Out of scope: upstream model weights distribution and hardware firmware issues (see hardware EOL docs).

Owners and responsibilities
---------------------------
- Runbook owner: eng-private-deployments -> Day-2 Ops (on-call rotation).
- Primary validation engineer: named in run execution tickets (must be an SRE or runtime engineer).
- Customer communication: Account Success + Solutions Engineering for production-facing tests.
- Rollback authority: On-call SE + PM for the affected customer.

Prerequisites and testbed configuration
--------------------------------------
1) A staging cluster that mirrors the customer's tenant topology (same VM/GPU mix, same KV shard counts).
2) Traffic generator: our workload-replay harness (versioned) with 7-day sample of request distribution.
3) Telemetry collection: fine-grained sampling of kv.op.latency, kv.miss_rate, kv.consistency_violations, model.token-latency per route.
4) SLO baseline snapshot: capture 72-hour pre-test baseline for latency P50/P90/P99 and error_rate.

Validation matrix (high level)
-----------------------------
This matrix maps scenario -> validation steps -> automated guardrails -> rollback triggers.

| Scenario | Core validation steps | Guardrail metrics (auto) | Rollback trigger (immediate) | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Node eviction (planned) | 1) Drain node; 2) Observe KV rebalancer; 3) Verify cache hot-keys rehydrate within 2x baseline cold-start | kv.miss_rate increase <= 3x baseline for <= 10m; kv.rebalance_errors == 0 | kv.rebalance_errors > 0 for 2m OR sustained kv.miss_rate > 3x baseline for 15m | Simulate with --evict-delay=30s to emulate graceful drain |
| Forced eviction (stress) | 1) Trigger eviction pressure; 2) Monitor per-tenant tail-latency and decode error counts; 3) Run consistency validator for sample request ids | model.tail_latency P99 increase <= 1.5x baseline; consistency_violations == 0 | any consistency_violations > 0 OR sustained P99 > 2x baseline for 10m | Run in blue/green canary ring first |
| Cross-node invalidation bug | 1) Introduce invalidation race via concurrent write tests; 2) Run deterministic replay; 3) Check idempotency and KV read-after-write | read_after_write_success_rate >= 99.99% | read_after_write_success_rate < 99.9% OR more than 1 data-mismatch in 100k ops | Use small blast radius and assert end-to-end hash checksums |
| Model shard hot-swap | 1) Swap model shard binary; 2) Check KV shard affinity and cached embeddings validity; 3) Run 1k query golden set | embedding_mismatch_count == 0; kv.miss_rate acceptable | embedding_mismatch_count > 0 OR error_rate increase > 0.5% sustained | Prefer staged swap with canary traffic (5%) |

Validation steps (detailed)
--------------------------
1. Baseline capture (pre-test window):
   - Capture metrics for 72 hours: latency P50/P90/P99, token-throughput, kv.miss_rate, kv.hit_latency, kv.rebalance_time.
   - Create a baseline artifact (JSON) and attach to the test run ticket.

2. Canary (ringed) execution:
   - Select 5% of tenant traffic in the staging cluster.
   - Run the scenario for a 20–30 minute burn-in while collecting full telemetry.
   - Run the deterministic replay tool against canary nodes and run the consistency checker.

3. Full run (if canary succeeds):
   - Execute global change during maintenance window.
   - Keep mitigation toggles ready: auto-evacuation-disabled, kv-rebalancer-throttle=0.2, eviction-pressure-safety=true.

Automated guardrails and alerting rules
--------------------------------------
- kv.consistency_violations: alert - critical when count >= 1 for 1m in production tenant rings.
- kv.rebalance_errors: alert - page on >= 1 in 2m during rebalances.
- model.tail_latency.p99: warn at 1.5x baseline, critical at 2x baseline.
- Auto-fallback job: if kv.rebalance_errors triggered, system will prevent next stage rollout and open rollback ticket (auto-created).

Rollback matrix (decision tree)
------------------------------
- If consistency_violations detected: immediate rollback of the change that modified cache topology or invalidation semantics. Steps:
  1) Pause routing to changed nodes (traffic manager -> weight=0).
  2) Revert config / restore previous runtime artifact.
  3) Run fast-integrity-scan (checksums on 1M sampled kv keys).
  4) If checksums pass, progressively re-enable traffic at 10/30/60 minute increments.
  5) If checksums fail, escalate to on-call runtime lead and open SE/Customer incident.

- If sustained latency degradation without data mismatches: roll forward mitigation (throttle rebalancer, increase cache size) for hot fix; only rollback if mitigation fails within 30m.

Runbook: executing a validation run (operator steps)
--------------------------------------------------
1. Create a run ticket in JIRA project PRIV-RUN with tags: kv-cache, chaos-validation, <customer-id>.
2. Attach baseline artifact and planned scenario script.
3. Perform canary run and annotate observations in the ticket.
4. If canary passes, schedule full run during maintenance window and notify stakeholders (30m/10m/5m warnings).
5. Execute full run and keep the rollback playbook open in parallel.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail)
------------------------------
- Pass if:
  - No consistency_violations observed during canary and full run.
  - model.tail_latency.p99 increase <= 1.5x baseline for <= 30 minutes after change.
  - kv.rebalance_errors remain == 0.
- Fail if any consistency_violations occur or if automated rollback triggers fire.

Telemetry and sampling guidance
------------------------------
- Sampling rate: kv.operation_trace sample=1/1000 by default; increase to 1/100 for any validation run.
- Mandatory logs to collect: kv.op.trace (json), cache-shard-metrics.csv (1s rollups), node-procstats (30s).
- Attach generated trace artifacts to the JIRA ticket; preserve for 90 days for postmortem analysis.

CLI and example commands
------------------------
- Start a canary with the replay harness:
  ./replay --tenant <tenant-id> --ratio 0.05 --trace-sampling 0.01 --scenario kv-invalidation-race --output run-<date>.json

- Trigger a forced eviction (staging only):
  redwood-admin evict --shard <shard-id> --pressure 0.9 --duration 300s

- Run the integrity checksum utility (sampled):
  ./kv-checksum --cluster staging --sample 100000 --output checksum-<date>.ndjson

Appendix: common failure patterns and mitigations
------------------------------------------------
- Pattern: slow rehydrate after drain -> Mitigation: pre-warm hot-key loader and increase kv.rebalance_window to 60s.
- Pattern: transient read-after-write mismatch under high-write bursts -> Mitigation: apply write-ack serialisation window or enable stronger consistency mode for affected tenant.
- Pattern: configuration drift between nodes -> Mitigation: run node-config-compare across cluster and auto-fix drifted keys.

References
----------
- See runtime state migration playbook: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook-2025.json
- Incremental upgrade guidance: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/incremental-stateful-upgrade-strategy-2027.json
